In Situation <REF_0001> the functor
<MATH_0001> satisfies openness of versality.

We have to show the following. Given a scheme <MATH_0001> locally of finite type over
<MATH_0002>, given <MATH_0003>, and given a finite type point <MATH_0004> such that
<MATH_0005> is versal at <MATH_0006>, after replacing <MATH_0007> by an open neighbourhood
of <MATH_0008> we have that <MATH_0009> is versal at every finite type point of <MATH_0010>.
Write <MATH_0011>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
First case: <MATH_0012>. Then we can first replace <MATH_0013> by
<MATH_0014>. Hence we see that <MATH_0015>
and the morphism <MATH_0016> is versal at <MATH_0017>.
By More on Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0001>
this means that <MATH_0018> is smooth at <MATH_0019>.
Since the set of a points where a morphism is smooth is open,
we can after shrinking <MATH_0020> assume <MATH_0021> is smooth.
Then the same lemma tells us that <MATH_0022> is versal at every
point as desired.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Second case: <MATH_0023>. Write <MATH_0024> as in
Formal Spaces, Lemma <REF_0002>.
By Lemma <REF_0003> we may assume <MATH_0025>
is a smooth morphism of formal algebraic spaces. It follows immediately
that <MATH_0026> is versal at all finite type points of <MATH_0027>.
Let <MATH_0028>, <MATH_0029>, and <MATH_0030> witness the compatibility between <MATH_0031>
and <MATH_0032>. We see that <MATH_0033> is smooth as a
base change of <MATH_0034>. Since <MATH_0035> is the completion of
<MATH_0036> this implies that <MATH_0037> is smooth at all
points of <MATH_0038>
by the already used More on Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0004>.
Since the set of smooth points of a morphism is open, we see that
the closed set of points <MATH_0039> where <MATH_0040> is not smooth
does not meet <MATH_0041>. Since <MATH_0042> is proper and
hence closed, we see that <MATH_0043> is a closed
subset not meeting <MATH_0044>. Hence after shrinking <MATH_0045> we may assume
<MATH_0046>, i.e., <MATH_0047> is smooth. By the discussion in the previous
paragraph this exactly means that <MATH_0048> is versal at all finite type
points of <MATH_0049> not contained in <MATH_0050> and the proof is complete.
